To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tolerance to the analgesia produced from electrical stimulation of the midbrain periaqueductual gray is mediated by environmental conditional stimulus (CS).

the analgesia produced in rats by electrical brain stimulation is attenuated with repeated stimulation, and that this tolerance is extinguished when the CS associated with stimulation is presented in the absence of stimulation.

(a) environmental CSs are necessary for tolerance to analgesic effects produced by electrical brain stimulation, and (b) tolerance to brain-stimulation analgesic is specific to the environmental context in which it was produced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a behavioral model of tolerance and the analysis of its neural mechanisms.
a new approach to the study of the mechanisms of tolerance to analgesic effects produced by electrical stimulation of the brain.
the effects of electrical stimulation (brain stimulation) on pain and pain behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brainstem is not a site of action for morphine tolerance, but that tolerance to the analgesia produced there by brain-stimulation may be mediated by environmental CSs.
tolerance to the analgesia produced in the periaquedutal gray is mediated by the environment in which the analgesia is produced.
the analgesic properties of the brain-stimulation analgesic system are not affected by the environmental conditions in which the stimulation is administered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tolerance to analgesics can be produced by environmental conditional stimuli, and that tolerance can be extinguished by omitting the CS in the absence of the unconditioned stimulus.
tolerance to analgesic effect of electrical stimulation of PAG is mediated by environmental CSs.
tolerance to the analgesia produced in the brainstem is not a result of the development of a conditioned response to the environment but is a direct effect of the stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we demonstrated that tolerance to the analgesia effects of electrical stimulation in the periaquedactal gray can be conditioned to environmental stimuli.
tolerance to the analgesia produced in the periaquedutal gray can be conditioned to the environment and extinguished by removing the conditioned stimulus.
we have shown that the effects of brain stimulation can be conditioned, and that this conditioning can be used to study the neurophysiology of tolerance to analgesics.
